headline: Delayed updates on Langsford erosion repair and cemetery business support to the October meeting; approved June minutes.
summary: Members reported on a stone restoration paid by DPW for $3791.00 and on the treasurer's balances. Several updates were delayed until the October meeting. Members also reviewed columbaria examples and a pending state bill on natural organic reduction.

City-Owned Cemeteries Advisory Committee  
Tuesday, 8 September 2026 from 5:30pm to 7:00pm 
The Rose Baker Center for Aging Well  
2-RBSC - Upstairs Conference Room 
6 Manuel F. Lewis St., Gloucester, MA 01930 
 
MINUTES 
Members Present: Sandy Barry, Matt Murray, Melissa Hobbs, Cindi Williams, and 
Christine Maney               Guest: Kathy Clark 
 
The meeting was not recorded due to technical recording problems. We continued with the meeting since our 
agendas state the following, “Please note that the in-person meeting will not be suspended or terminated if 
technological problems interrupt the remote connection.” 
 
1. Minutes for 16 June 2026 were approved.  
 
2. Sandy gave an update on the status of current restorations. Gravesite Preservation (Rob Surabian) 
completed the restoration of 10 damaged stones in First Parish Burial Ground caused by a dead tree falling 
during a winter storm in Dec 2022. DPW paid for the restoration, $3791.00. 
 
The restoration of American Revolutionary War veteran Josiah Choate (DOD 1798) has been delayed due 
to funding and the need to clear fallen trees on the fire road that leads from Concord Street to Second Parish 
burial ground. Rob had told Sandy that he would look to see if there was an alternate path for his equipment 
in order to reach the cemetery.  The restoration work was to be completed in the cemetery due to the size of 
the stone and the remoteness of the cemetery. Sandy was going to speak to DPW about clearing the fire 
road. During the discussion Choate funding possibilities included approaching the Sons of the American 
Revolution (SAR) and Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR). 
 
3. Melissa delayed the update on erosion repair at Langsford until the October monthly meeting. 
 
4. Chris gave CCAC’s Treasurer's Report as of 8 September 2026.

5. Chris shared with the committee that DPW assumes that the 2027 DPW CCAC Budget will remain at 
$5,000. 
 
6. Due to a prior commitment, an update by Carol on her meeting with Gloucester’s IT head, John Gillis, to 
discuss the DPW files and backups was delayed until the October monthly meeting. 
 
7. Due to a prior commitment, an update by Carol on contacting Mike Hale and the Mayor letting them know 
that CCAC is looking into the possibility of local businesses contributing financial support yearly to the city 
cemeteries and/or adopting a city cemetery providing financial support was delayed until the October 
monthly meeting. 
 
8. Due to a prior commitment, an update by Carol on the status of her volunteering to create a written 
presentation to use when approaching businesses asking for their financial support for the city cemeteries 
was delayed until the October monthly meeting. 
 
9. In late June Chris spoke to Gloucester’s CFO, Conor MacCorkle, and was told the city does have tax-
exempt status much like a 501c3.  After explaining to him that CCAC has been unable to apply for several 
grants because of the non-profit stipulation, he said that the city can receive tax deductible gifts and he 
would send Chris copies of the city’s tax-exempt ID. Conor also stated that the city cannot receive Vimeo or 
PayPal donations. 
 
Since meeting with Conor in June, Conor has stepped down as Gloucester’s CFO and Chris is working with 
the city’s finance department to secure the city’s tax-exempt ID. 
 
10. Chris is currently waiting to hear back from Cape Ann Savings’ Marketing Department on their civic 
donations and support.
This meeting is recorded 
 
The listing of matters is those reasonably anticipated by the Chair which may be discussed at the meeting.  Not all items listed may in fact be discussed and other items not 
listed may also be brought up for discussion to the extent permitted by law. 
11. Melissa gave the committee an update on what she knew with respect to the Gloucester Historical 
Commission’s application to the MA Historical Commission. She said Susan Morreale applied to the MA 
Historical Commission in nominating Lane's Cove Landing and the surrounding historic area to the National 
Register of Historic Places. The area in question includes Cove Hill Cemetery. John Lane donated the area 
for Cove Hill Cemetery after the death of his daughter (Deborah Lane, DOD 1729). John Lane had owned 
over 60 acres in Lanesville. It was mentioned to her that state funds would be available if the application 
was accepted but no funding details were offered. Melissa asked if CCAC would submit a letter of support 
for this application and Sandy volunteered to write the letter of support. 
 
Melissa also mentioned the Lanesville community project spearheaded by the Lane’s Cove Historical 
Association (LCHA) to place a plaque in Lane’s Cove honoring John and Dorcas Lane is moving ahead. 
 
12. Matt prepared and distributed to members of the committee a 7-page pictorial handout that offered examples 
of local columbaria: Cedar Grove, Dorchester, MA and St. Joseph’s Cemetery, West Roxbury, MA.  
 
He discussed the pictorial handout pointing out niche design (cremains compartments), niche covers 
(outward sealing materials used and engraving), supporting structures (wall or free standing), foundations 
(base structures), protective tops and caps (drainage), and landscape features.  Members learned a lot from 
the visual display and discussion. 
 
Matt was asked to research pricing: 
a) The cost of a niche panel (a unit of multiple niches)? 
b) The cost of installing a niche panel (a unit of multiple niches)? 
c) The cemetery cost to a person or family interested in purchasing a niche? 
d) The cost for a niche burial? 
e) Do cemeteries require perpetual care fees for a niche? If so, how much? 
 
13. New Business 
 
a) Kathy remarked that on social media it was noted that people were using the water at city cemeteries to 
wash their cars during Gloucester’s water restriction mandate. 
 
b) Cindi had nothing to report but is still following the bill, Senate, No. 2851 
  “The committee on Public Health, to whom was referred the petitions (accompanied by bill, Senate, No. 1611) 
of Jacob R. Oliveira and Paul W. Mark for legislation to offer natural organic reduction as an environmentally-
friendly burial alternative; and (accompanied by bill, Senate, No. 1612) of Jacob R. Oliveira for legislation 
relative to burial alternatives that protect the environment, report the accompanying bill (Senate, No. 2851).”  
 
 
 
 
Meeting was adjourned at 7:10 pm 
Respectfully submitted, 
Christine Maney
